claims.text: Lattice distortion is the primary microstructural mechanism governing enhanced mechanical strength in refractory high-entropy alloys at high temperatures.
Lattice distortion is the primary microstructural mechanism governing altered thermoelastic behavior in refractory high-entropy alloys at high temperatures.
The initial materials are as-cast or heat-treated refractory HEAs containing multiple principal elements.
A tailored heat treatment or slight compositional modification can reduce lattice distortion while precipitate density and grain size are held constant.
The proposed comparison applies at temperatures of at least 1000°C under controlled stress or strain cycling and thermal cycling.
Multiple principal elements induce excessive lattice distortion.
Lattice distortion creates localized stress fields.
The localized stress fields produced by lattice distortion impede dislocation mobility.
Impeded dislocation mobility improves high-temperature mechanical strength.
Lattice distortion modifies high-temperature thermoelastic response.
Reducing lattice distortion lowers barriers to dislocation motion.
A sample with reduced lattice distortion will have lower yield strength than the higher-distortion baseline under identical high-temperature conditions.
A sample with reduced lattice distortion will exhibit different elastic modulus and thermal expansion coefficients from the higher-distortion baseline.
Standard heat treatment maximizes the inherent lattice distortion of the baseline refractory HEA.
XRD peak broadening and TEM can quantitatively characterize lattice distortion for this comparison.
Failure to observe a statistically significant decrease in yield strength or a change in thermoelastic parameters after reducing lattice distortion would falsify the dominance hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that only lattice distortion is varied, but one permitted intervention is a compositional adjustment, which necessarily varies composition and may change additional material properties beyond lattice distortion.
